oracle.project: Zhang (2008), Causal reasoning with ancestral graphs, Definition 8 (visibility) and Lemmas 9-10; Shpitser & Pearl (2006) ID on the confounded ADMG
oracle.generator: hand-derived from the generating DAGs named in each case; the numeric truth of every identified case, and the soundness of the reduction over all small DAGs, is checked by exact SCM enumeration in crates/antecedent-identify/src/mag_id_bruteforce.rs
oracle.scope: single-treatment E[Y | do(T)] on a directed/bidirected MAG or the MAG completions of a PAG. Sound, not complete: 'refused' is not a proof of non-identifiability. The complete PAG algorithm (IDP; Jaber, Zhang & Bareinboim 2019) is not implemented.

cases.generating_dag: T <- L -> Y, T -> Y (L latent)
cases.reason: nothing points into T, so T -> Y is invisible and P(y | t) is confounded by L

cases.generating_dag: T -> M -> Y, T <- L -> Y (L latent)
cases.reason: the inducing path T <- L -> Y appears in the MAG as an invisible T -> Y; the MAG also represents DAGs with a confounded direct effect, so the front-door functional is not licensed from the MAG
T is an ancestor of its spouse Y (almost-directed cycle); hold this graph as an Admg
R points into T and is not adjacent to Y

cases.generating_dag: D -> C <- L -> T, C -> Y, T -> Y (L latent)
cases.reason: D is not adjacent to Y and D -> C <-> T is a collider path into T whose interior C is a parent of Y

cases.generating_dag: T -> M -> Y, M -> B -> Y, A -> Y, T <- L1 -> A <- L2 -> B (L1, L2 latent)
cases.reason: blocking T <-> A -> Y needs A, which opens T <-> A <-> B -> Y, and B descends from the mediator: no adjustment set. Every directed edge is visible, so ID separates T from its child M
Y is not a descendant of T in any represented DAG: E[Y | do(t)] = E[Y]; no set m-separates T and Y, so adjustment cannot say so
the completions are the invisible T -> Y (refused) and T <-> Y (null effect)
